posts.title: The Draw, Explained
posts.excerpt: Club secretary Ingrid Solberg outlines how the weekly draw places names on the morning sheet.
posts.content:
Every Thursday evening at 18:00, the weekend morning sheet opens for entries. By the time the list closes for the Friday draw at 12:00, dozens of member names have been logged in the ledger at the club office. For new members and long-standing four-balls alike, understanding how these tee times are allocated is part of the rhythm of life at Misora Links.

The morning sheet is intentionally constrained. Between 06:40 and 09:00 every Tuesday through Sunday, exactly fifteen tee times are called at ten-minute intervals. Because our club maintains a strict cap of 640 members, demand for early weekend starts along the dunes is always steady. Rather than rewarding whoever writes in first, the Friday draw is how names are placed on the opening hours of turf and tide.

When entries close on Friday at noon, club secretary Ingrid Solberg oversees the draw in the office at 1 Starter's Lane. The draw reviews submissions based on recent playing history, giving gentle preference to members who were left off the sheet during the preceding weekend. Foursomes and twosomes are organized into the fifteen available slots, matching requested windows as closely as the numbers allow. Results are posted to the clubhouse board and distributed by email by 13:00 every Friday.

Once the draw is announced, players are expected to confirm their participation. If illness, travel, or unforeseen responsibilities disrupt your weekend plans, club policy requires that cancellations be phoned or emailed to the office by 18:00 on the evening prior to play. This deadline allows golfers on the reserve list time to arrange their equipment, coordinate with caddies, and travel along the coast road to Westerby Point for first light.

On Saturday and Sunday mornings, the quiet mechanics of the draw come to life on the ground. At 06:20, head starter Tomas Reyes-Hale unlocks the starter's box, prepares his clipboard, and sets out the morning sheet beside a thermos. Players begin gathering on the gravel path and practice green as dawn lifts over the old pines. Because weekend morning play requires carry bags exclusively, players travel light, shoulder their clubs, and prepare for a round paced at four hours and ten minutes.

At 06:40 sharp, the first group is called to the tee. Whether it is the 06:40 four stepping up to hit their opening drives into the morning mist or a member guiding an invited guest for their first glimpse of the inward dunes, the order set by the Friday draw keeps the start calm and unhurried. By 09:00, all fifteen morning groups are underway, leaving the links quiet until the afternoon walk-up sheet commences at 11:30.

The draw is more than an administrative exercise; it is the civic framework of Misora Links. By sharing the prime hours of the week through a published sheet, we keep the uncrowded fairways, mutual respect, and quiet dignity that have defined our coastal community since 1961.
